action: Scoping: the public cannot respond to the Planning Inspectorate directly. Ask your parish clerk and Vale ward councillor to press for specific items in the Environmental Statement: field-level land grades, viewpoints from village conservation areas, HGV routes avoiding villages, cumulative assessment with the reservoir construction programme, and battery storage siting and fire safety
Register for Planning Inspectorate email updates on EN0110044 and the developer's updates; write to the developer at info@cearnsolarfarm.co.uk or Freepost CEARN SOLAR FARM
Join Protect the Vale's update list; ask your parish to engage with the Vale's Oxfordshire Association of Local Councils route
Respond to the developer's Stage 2 consultation, the main chance to shape the layout and cable route. It is no longer a legal requirement but the developer says it will run it
Register as an Interested Party with a Relevant Representation on the PINS page within the advertised window. Only Interested Parties can take full part in the examination
Lobby the Vale and Oxfordshire County Council for strong Local Impact Reports; make written submissions and speak at open floor hearings

Write to MPs and councillors (see representatives) and to the DESNZ Secretary of State by post. Focus on planning matters: landscape, heritage setting, farmland grades, flood risk, traffic, noise, ecology, battery safety, cumulative effects
Judicial review in the High Court under section 118 of the Planning Act 2008, on legal and procedural grounds only (general information, not legal advice)

note: The Vale planning committee and its speaking rules do not apply to Cearn because it is an NSIP decided by the Secretary of State
